<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with vivid, disciplined framing. PRO built a strong sovereignty/equity case ("objection is not title," "the water still goes downstream, the years do not") and landed the best hit of the debate by forcing CON to admit that if Cairo rejects a binding rule Ethiopia fills anyway — which blunted CON's model into something closer to PRO's world and let PRO brand the process as "the stop-switch renamed verification." But CON did more decisive work overall. First, CON pre-empted the veto frame with a concrete mechanism (pre-agreed hydrological trigger, drought release floor, arbitration on a fixed clock) and answered PRO's questions squarely with the honest "yes, Ethiopia fills, but as the party with law rather than a rifle behind it," preserving a real distinction from the motion as written. Second, CON extracted PRO's [A4.3] concession that Ethiopia should slow if inflow collapses, then converted the whole debate into the single question PRO could not answer well: who verifies the trigger? "A duty with no auditor" and "trust us, we'll audit ourselves" are clean, memorable reasons to reject a self-certified timeline. Third, CON's asymmetry-of-errors weighing (deferred megawatt-hours are recoverable; a failed harvest and a dry Khartoum tap are not) gave the clearer decision rule, and PRO's rejoinder that Aswan's reserve exists to be spent during a known fill answered but did not defeat the tail-risk framing. CON's use of the 2015 Declaration of Principles was ordinary, plausible background rather than fake precision, and it usefully reframed reciprocity. Offsetting CON's edge: three of its turns were clipped for exceeding the cap, repeatedly losing its closing weighing sentences, while PRO was consistently tighter and more economical. That execution cost keeps the margin competitive rather than solid.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's exploitation of PRO's answer in [A4.3]: by getting PRO to concede Ethiopia must slow in extreme drought, CON reduced the motion to "who verifies the emergency," then argued the party holding reservoir, turbines and gauges cannot be sole judge — a reframe PRO's closing answered only by insisting the rulebook is unsigned.</best_rebuttal>
